html:
Two invasions of Korea by Japan, in 1592 and 1597, ordered by Toyotomi Hideyoshi. His aim was to march through Korea and conquer Ming China.

In 1592 about 150,000 Japanese troops, many armed with muskets, landed at Busan and took Seoul and Pyongyang within weeks. The Joseon king fled north. Then the tide turned:

  • Admiral Yi Sun-sin won a string of sea battles, partly with armoured turtle ships, and cut Japanese supply lines.
  • Korean guerrilla bands, including armed monks, rose across the country.
  • A large Ming army came to Korea's aid in 1593.

A long stalemate and failed peace talks followed. Japan invaded again in 1597 but was held in the south. When Hideyoshi died in 1598 his generals withdrew, and Yi was killed in the last sea battle.

Korea was devastated: towns burned, palaces such as Gyeongbokgung lost, many potters and craftsmen carried off to Japan. The war drained the Ming and weakened Hideyoshi's heirs, opening the way for Tokugawa Ieyasu.
sum: Two invasions of Korea by Japan, in 1592 and 1597, ordered by Toyotomi Hideyoshi. His aim was to march through Korea and conquer Ming China.
